nodes.title: Recognize Stronger-Result Meta-Options
nodes.when_to_use: When an option says that one of the remaining options is correct but a stronger result can be proven, especially when the question asks for the strongest statement
nodes.how_to_use: - Treat that meta-option as a serious candidate.

nodes.title: Prefer an Unlisted Strictly Stronger Conclusion
nodes.when_to_use: When a concrete option is true but the theorem or derivation gives a strictly stronger conclusion that is not exactly listed
nodes.how_to_use: - Choose the stronger-result meta-option.
avoid: Do not settle for the weaker concrete statement.

nodes.title: Rank Nested Conclusions by Strength
nodes.when_to_use: When the answer options are nested by logical or quantitative strength
nodes.how_to_use: - Rank the options explicitly before answering. Finite-time blowup is stronger than merely not globally bounded; positive stable growth is stronger than ordinary unboundedness; sharper constants, rates, exceptional-set bounds, endpoint inclusion, and full equivalences are stronger than weaker asymptotic versions.

nodes.title: Compare Every Option Before Selection
nodes.how_to_use: - Compare all options before committing and select the strongest statement justified by the visible question and hypotheses.
avoid: Do not choose a nearby option merely because it is plausible when it is weaker, overstrong, or misses an equality case.

nodes.title: Track Exact Quantifiers
nodes.when_to_use: When options or hypotheses use quantifiers such as there exists, for every, if and only if, or exactly when
nodes.how_to_use: - Preserve each quantifier exactly while comparing the theorem with the options.

nodes.title: Require Support for Converse and Classification Claims
nodes.when_to_use: When considering a converse, realization, classification, if-and-only-if, or exactly-all claim
nodes.how_to_use: - Require the visible theorem or derivation to prove the added direction or classification.
avoid: Do not add converse, realization, or classification claims to a one-way implication.

nodes.title: Detect Weakened Conclusions
nodes.when_to_use: When an option drops a characterization, equality clause, or full equivalence from the justified conclusion
nodes.how_to_use: - Treat the omission as a genuine weakening when ranking the options.

nodes.title: Detect Overstated Conclusions
nodes.when_to_use: When an option upgrades regularity, removes scale restrictions, or changes an existential statement into a universal one
nodes.how_to_use: - Mark the option as stronger than the theorem actually proves.
avoid: Do not silently strengthen regularity, scope, scale, or quantifiers.

nodes.title: Verify Both Directions of an Equivalence
nodes.when_to_use: For biconditional or equivalence questions
nodes.how_to_use: - Verify necessity and sufficiency separately.
avoid: Reject a condition that is merely necessary or merely sufficient when equivalence is required.

nodes.title: Check the Exact Threshold Sign
nodes.when_to_use: For threshold conditions whose options differ by the sign of a parameter
nodes.how_to_use: - Verify the exact sign, such as distinguishing \(\mu_0\) from \(-\mu_0\).

nodes.title: Rank Logical Scope by Strength
nodes.when_to_use: When options differ by for every versus for sufficiently large, or by local versus global domains
nodes.how_to_use: - Rank the statements by logical strength and match the sharpest version justified by the theorem.

nodes.title: Match Every Hypothesis and Domain Restriction
nodes.when_to_use: When matching a theorem-shaped option to the visible hypotheses
nodes.how_to_use: - Verify every assumption and the exact domain before accepting the conclusion.
avoid: Do not accept a distractor that preserves the theorem's shape while altering a required assumption.

nodes.title: Check Equality, Extremality, and Family Scope
nodes.when_to_use: When options differ on an equality case, an extremal condition, or whether the result covers the full family or only a restricted subfamily
nodes.how_to_use: - Match each boundary and family-scope clause exactly.

nodes.title: Return One Option Label
nodes.when_to_use: After completing the mathematical comparison
nodes.how_to_use: - Output the final answer as the single option label only.
avoid: Do not append explanation outside the required graph_usage sidecar.

nodes.title: Distinguish Global from Localized Conclusions
nodes.when_to_use: When a conclusion holds only after localization, completion, or at each prime or scale
nodes.how_to_use: - Treat that conclusion as weaker than an unqualified global equivalence.
avoid: Do not promote a localized or completed equivalence to an unqualified global one.

nodes.title: Compare Estimate Exponents, Indices, and Constants
nodes.when_to_use: For estimate-heavy options
nodes.how_to_use: - Compare the exponent, derivative-index range, constants, and every stated parameter dependence.

nodes.title: Reject Broader Non-Equivalent Conditions
nodes.when_to_use: When one option replaces an exact condition with a broader one, such as congruence modulo a divisor instead of modulo the full modulus
nodes.how_to_use: - Compare the admitted cases and require the same solution set for an equivalence.
avoid: Do not accept the broader condition unless the stated domain collapses all extra cases.

nodes.title: Check Strict versus Non-Strict Endpoints
nodes.when_to_use: When threshold or range options differ by strict versus non-strict inequalities
nodes.how_to_use: - Distinguish \(<\) from \(\le\) and verify whether the endpoint is included.

nodes.title: Assign the Equality Case to the Correct Regime
nodes.when_to_use: When a threshold separates positive, zero, and negative parameter regimes
nodes.how_to_use: - Determine explicitly which regime contains the equality case.

nodes.title: Compare Estimate Correction Terms
nodes.when_to_use: When quantitative options differ by rates, exceptional-set bounds, logarithmic factors, or additive terms
nodes.how_to_use: - Compare every correction term and quantitative refinement exactly.

nodes.title: Compare Directionality and Convergence Mode
nodes.when_to_use: When estimate options differ by one-sided versus two-sided notation or pointwise versus uniform convergence
nodes.how_to_use: - Preserve the stated directionality and convergence mode exactly.
